patent.title: Antigen binding proteins to proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin type 9 (PCSK9)
patent.family_note: Experimental claim-focused analysis of claims 19 and 29. Other claims in the same patent may have different legal status; the current V0.7 Ledger has no first-class claim-set rights-control object.

knowledge_origin.description: This pressure test does not reconstruct the complete original R&D genealogy of the PCSK9 antibody program.

technology.problem: Reduce LDL cholesterol by preventing PCSK9 from degrading LDL receptors.
technology.mechanism: A functionally defined genus of monoclonal antibodies that bind specified PCSK9 residues/epitopes and block the PCSK9-LDLR interaction.

value_carriers.name: Praluent (alirocumab)
value_carriers.description: The parties stipulated infringement of claims 19 and 29; this is a direct claim-set-to-product mapping. The relevant claim set was later held invalid for lack of enablement.

value_links.note: Historical infringement/implementation mapping. It does not imply the claim set remained enforceable at T0.
Product-level scale evidence in the U.S.; not patent-level value.

value_metrics.note: Do not attribute or apportion this product revenue to the patent or claim set. The same product metric may appear in more than one patent ledger and must never be summed across patents.

gaps.description: Praluent product sales and commercial scale cannot be apportioned to this patent or claim set from the public record.

V0.7 records R4 implementation/scale but has no structured field showing that claims 19 and 29 was invalid for lack of enablement at T0. Claim-level rights-control status is therefore hidden in evidence/notes rather than represented as a comparable state.
needed_evidence: validity/enforceability field keyed to claim set
scope-type field for functional genus claims

notes: Non-award V0.8 pressure-test ledger. R4 describes confirmed historical implementation plus commercial scale; it does NOT mean the analyzed claim set was enforceable at T0. claims 19 and 29 was held invalid for lack of enablement. Product revenue must not be inherited by the patent. The Supreme Court also distinguishes separate 2011 sequence-specific product patents that were not at issue.
